title: 12th Session of India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission held in New Delhi
subtitle:
Minister of State Shri Jitin Prasada and Belarusian Foreign Minister Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov co-chair the Session
Both sides review bilateral cooperation and discuss measures to strengthen trade, economic and investment relations
India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum held alongside the Session to explore opportunities for greater business engagement
body_text: The 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation was held on 16th November 2026 in New Delhi. Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation, while Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus H.E. Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov led the Belarusian delegation. The Session reviewed the progress of bilateral cooperation and discussed measures to further strengthen trade, economic and investment relations between the two countries. Both sides appreciated the longstanding and friendly relations between India and Belarus and highlighted the importance of regular exchanges, closer institutional engagement and greater participation of businesses in taking the partnership forward. Discussions covered several important areas of economic cooperation, with a focus on expanding bilateral trade and investment. Both sides also discussed the Roadmap for Cooperation for 2027–2031 as an important step towards identifying future priorities and providing direction to bilateral economic engagement. Key sectors discussed included industry, financial and banking services, agriculture and food processing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, tourism, education, culture, science and technology, construction and customs cooperation. The Protocol of the 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission was signed by both Co-Chairs, reaffirming the commitment of the two countries to deepen bilateral cooperation. Addressing the business community, Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted India's growing economic and manufacturing capabilities and the opportunities they offer for closer engagement with Belarusian businesses. He emphasised that the longstanding friendship between the two countries provides a strong foundation for building practical and mutually beneficial economic partnerships. He also encouraged businesses to explore joint ventures, technology partnerships, investment opportunities and greater business-to-business engagement. Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted the potential for collaboration in areas such as pharmaceuticals, agricultural and industrial machinery, engineering, chemicals, digital technologies and scientific research. He also encouraged businesses from both countries to explore opportunities for market access, local partnerships, co-development and cooperation in emerging areas, including unmanned aerial systems and advanced manufacturing technologies. On the sidelines of the 12th Session of the Inter-Governmental Commission, the India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum was also organised in New Delhi on 16th November 2026. The Forum brought together business representatives, industry associations and government institutions from India and Belarus, providing an opportunity for direct interaction, exchange of ideas and exploration of new areas of trade, investment and commercial cooperation. The Forum saw participation from Belarusian companies representing diverse sectors, including automotive and agricultural machinery, mining equipment, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, microelectronics, banking, agriculture and engineering. Discussions focused on possibilities for joint ventures, technology transfer, localisation of manufacturing, research and development, and stronger supply-chain linkages. Opportunities in agricultural and civil unmanned aerial systems, pharmaceutical cooperation, mining equipment, water treatment technologies and food processing were also highlighted as potential areas for future collaboration. Both sides underlined the importance of maintaining regular engagement between their business communities and encouraged enterprises to take forward the opportunities identified during the discussions. India and Belarus agreed to continue working together to expand cooperation across the identified sectors and strengthen their economic partnership. Both sides also agreed to hold the 13th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission in 2027, with the dates and agenda to be finalised through diplomatic channels. *** Abhishek Dayal/ Abhijith Narayanan/ Ishita Biswas
